question.leadin: Answer the following about famous campaign slogans.
question.text: This 28th U.S. President first elected in 1912 ran on the slogan "he kept us out of war" to win reelection in 1916. Ironically, this man entered the war after the sinking of the Lusitania.
question.clue: He pushed for such legislation as the Keating-Owen act and the Underwood Tariff during his first term, as a realization of his program of "New Freedom."

swap.text: This American feminist, who was featured on the dollar coin, worked alongside Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucy Stone to create the National American Woman Suffrage Association.
swap.clue: Carrie Chapman Catt succeeded this Quaker in one post, and after this figure was barred from speaking at an Albany temperance meeting, she formed the Woman's New York State Temperance Society.

question.leadin: In 1920, this man ran for US President from a prison cell after being arrested for sedition.
question.text: Name this politician who, with "Big Bill" Haywood, helped found the Industrial Workers of the World.
question.clue: While participating in the ARU, this man was arrested for interfering with the mail, and was later represented by Clarence Darrow.

swap.leadin: Though he was convicted under the Espionage Act of 1917, his sentence was commuted in 1921 by President Harding.
swap.text: Identify this politician who ran for president five times, the last time from a prison cell.

question.text: This regiment of troops, led by Theodore Roosevelt, was victorious at the Battle of San Juan Hill. Alexander Proctor sculpted an equestrian statue of Roosevelt as the leader of this group of soldiers.
question.clue: One leader of this unit resigned from his post as Assistant Secretary of the Navy to join it.

swap.leadin: This anarchist was deported on the USS Buford alongside her lover, Alexander Berkman.
swap.text: Name this author of My Disillusionment in Russia who was radicalized by the Haymarket Affair. This Lithuanian immigrant was the publisher of Mother Earth.
swap.clue: She was boycotted by the British left after discussing her horror with Leninism in My Disillusionment in Russia, and her other writings include the periodical Mother Earth.

question.text: Alice Paul achieved earlier success after helping to pass this amendment, which gave women the right to vote.
question.clue: Specters of a new Force Bill were used by "antis" like Josephine Parker to argue against this legislation on racial grounds.

swap.leadin: The fatalities in this event were increased because a warning did not reach the 9th floor of the Asch Building in time.
swap.text: Identify this 1911 fire in which 146 workers died at the namesake New York clothing factory.
swap.clue: In the ensuing trial, Max Blanck and Isaac Harris were defended by Max Steuer, who caused their acquittal by making Kate Alterman repeat her testimony many times.

question.text: Early in his administration, Taft passed this tariff named for two Republican senators. It split Republicans into Progressive and Old Guard factions, leading to their loss in the elections of 1810.
question.clue: This law was later modified by the Underwood Act, and this law included a provision allowing for free trade with the Philippines.

swap.leadin: Examples include the construction of Hukuang Railroad and the refinancing of national debt in Haiti and Honduras.
swap.text: Name this William Howard Taft foreign policy that attempted to substitute investment for military force.
swap.clue: This policy aided in the overthrow of Jose Santos Zelaya and the installment of Adolfo Diaz in order to guarantee loans to the Nicaraguan government.

question.leadin: Answer the following about conservatives who didn't like the New Deal.
question.text: This Virginia Senator reportedly "came from his death bed" to the 1940 Democratic Convention to oppose FDR. A former Secretary of the Treasury under Wilson, he co-sponsored a controversial 1933 act that separated commercial and investment banking.
question.clue: In his sole Cabinet post he was appointed to replace William McAdoo and his most notable achievement in that office was the floating of a five billion dollar Victory Loan to liquidate World War I expenses.

swap.leadin: After the Venezuelan Crisis, the creator of this policy also added his namesake corollary to the Monroe Doctrine. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this policy created by Theodore Roosevelt which was used in acquiring the Panama Canal Zone. This term was paired in his motto with speaking softly.

question.leadin: This man used an enema machine to pump yogurt into the rectums of the patients at his Battle Creek Sanitorium.
question.text: Name this man who created a breakfast cereal called "Granula," whose blandness was intended to stop masturbation.
question.clue: At this physician's Battle Creek Sanitarium, he hosted three eugenics conferences for the Race Betterment Foundation. This physician developed a namesake variety of cornflakes that he served to his patients for breakfast.

swap.text: Mencken was represented by lawyers from this organization that, under the leadership of Roger Nash Baldwin, was also involved in the free speech cases Scopes, Gitlow v. New York, and US v. One Book Called Ulysses.
swap.clue: Helen Keller, a student of Perkins-trained Anne Sullivan, was a co-founder of this nonprofit, which financed the defense of teacher John T. Scopes in the Scopes Monkey Trial.

question.leadin: Answer the following about speakers on the Chautauqua circuit.
question.text: This frequent lecturer on the Chautauqua circuit later won the 1931 Nobel Peace Prize for her pacifist efforts during World War I. Toynbee Hall inspired an institution created by this activist.
question.answerHtml: Jane Addams [or Laura Jane Addams] (The institution was Hull House.)
question.clue: This activist advocated for recreation as a way of addressing juvenile delinquency in her book The Spirit of Youth and the City Streets.

swap.leadin: This company was accidentally sabotaged by "Joybubbles," a 7-year-old with perfect pitch; that feat was replicated by John Draper using Captain Crunch pirate whistles.
swap.text: Name this company that signed the Kingsbury Commitment to avoid one antitrust suit, but faced another in 1982. This company was purchased by its former subsidiary SBC in 2005.

question.leadin: This sentence appears just after a citation to Jacobson v. Massachussets and the assertion "The principle that sustains compulsory vaccination is broad enough to cover cutting the Fallopian tubes."
question.text: Give this curt six-word sentence that Oliver Wendell Holmes included in his majority opinion upholding the sterilization of Carrie Buck by the Commonwealth of Virginia.
question.answer: Three generations of imbeciles are enough

swap.text: Morris Hillquit derided the Socialist movement in America by using this phrase, a reference to Socialists boasting of the excellence of the namesake public service in Milwaukee.
swap.clue: This left-wing movement centered in Milwaukee, whose leaders included the Austrian-born Victor L. Berger and Emil Seidel.

question.text: Cocaine was first regulated by this 1914 U.S. law, which was driven by hysterical reports that mail-order blow was turning Southern blacks into unstoppable, white women-raping superhulks.

swap.text: This Interior Secretary was accused of interfering with coal-land claims in Alaska.
swap.clue: Pinchot feuded with this former mayor of Seattle, who tried to privatize certain Alaskan coal reserves as Taft's Secretary of the Interior.
